{"findings": [
  {
    "file": "app/models/optimized_image.rb",
    "line": 149,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Duplicate self.downsize definition silently replaces the width/height overload",
    "body": "The file now defines `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby does not support overloading: the second definition replaces the first, so the width/height version is dead code. Any caller using `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 100, 200)` will now hit the 3-argument method with `dimensions = 100` and `opts = 200`; `optimize` then calls `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer and raises NoMethodError (or, worse, builds `-resize 100` geometry with no aspect handling). The `force_aspect_ratio` path is likewise unreachable through the width/height form. This is an API break for an existing public class method. Use a single signature, or rename the dimensions form (e.g. `downsize_to_dimensions`), or accept both dimensions and options explicitly."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
    "line": 67,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Downsize loop ignores failure and never verifies the target size was reached",
    "body": "`OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false when the convert/gifsicle step fails, but the loop does not check the return value and never re-checks that the file shrank: it just calls downsize up to five times on the same path and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with whatever is on disk. If the image format has no extension on the tempfile path, if ImageMagick cannot parse `80%>` geometry, or if five 80% reductions simply cannot get under `max_image_size_kb`, the loop burns five CPU-heavy conversions and the oversized (or corrupted/truncated, since convert reads and writes the same file) image is uploaded and stored anyway, contrary to the configured limit. Additionally, because `from == to`, a failed convert can leave the tempfile truncated and that corrupt file is still uploaded. Break out on failure and, after the loop, reject the upload with a clear error if `tempfile.size` is still over the limit."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
    "line": 55,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types",
    "body": "The API download path was previously bounded by `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`; it is now hardcoded to `10.megabytes` regardless of the `type` parameter. This means non-image attachments (e.g. `type=attachment`) supplied via `url` can now make the server download up to 10MB even on sites configured with a much smaller limit, and each such upload may additionally trigger five downsize conversions. The enlarged download bound should be applied only when the target is an image (and arguably should still be a configurable/site-derived limit), not to every API upload."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js",
    "line": 182,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "api",
    "title": "Client validation no longer honors configured max size settings, including for attachments",
    "body": "Replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` raises the client-side limit for every upload type. Only images are downsized server-side; attachments are still rejected by the server against `max_attachment_size_kb`. On a site configured with, say, a 1MB attachment limit, an 8MB PDF now passes `validateUploadedFile`, is uploaded, and only then fails with a server error. The message in `displayErrorForUpload` (line 246) has the same problem: the 413 case hardcodes 10MB and will report the wrong limit whenever the web-server threshold differs. The larger limit should be scoped to images (and ideally still derived from the site settings), leaving attachment limits unchanged."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
    "line": 64,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "test_gap",
    "title": "No tests cover the new automatic-downsize behavior",
    "body": "The PR adds a new synchronous downsize loop plus a new `OptimizedImage.downsize` signature/overload, but no specs are included. There are no tests for: reaching the target size after N reductions, the loop giving up after 5 attempts, conversion failure (return false) being surfaced, the API-URL path, or animated GIFs via `downsize_instructions_animated`. The zero-arity/argument ambiguity between the two `downsize` definitions would also be caught by a simple unit test and currently is not."
  }
]}

findings.title: Duplicate self.downsize definition silently replaces the width/height overload
findings.body: The file now defines `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby does not support overloading: the second definition replaces the first, so the width/height version is dead code. Any caller using `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 100, 200)` will now hit the 3-argument method with `dimensions = 100` and `opts = 200`; `optimize` then calls `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer and raises NoMethodError (or, worse, builds `-resize 100` geometry with no aspect handling). The `force_aspect_ratio` path is likewise unreachable through the width/height form. This is an API break for an existing public class method. Use a single signature, or rename the dimensions form (e.g. `downsize_to_dimensions`), or accept both dimensions and options explicitly.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failure and never verifies the target size was reached
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false when the convert/gifsicle step fails, but the loop does not check the return value and never re-checks that the file shrank: it just calls downsize up to five times on the same path and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with whatever is on disk. If the image format has no extension on the tempfile path, if ImageMagick cannot parse `80%>` geometry, or if five 80% reductions simply cannot get under `max_image_size_kb`, the loop burns five CPU-heavy conversions and the oversized (or corrupted/truncated, since convert reads and writes the same file) image is uploaded and stored anyway, contrary to the configured limit. Additionally, because `from == to`, a failed convert can leave the tempfile truncated and that corrupt file is still uploaded. Break out on failure and, after the loop, reject the upload with a clear error if `tempfile.size` is still over the limit.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types
findings.body: The API download path was previously bounded by `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`; it is now hardcoded to `10.megabytes` regardless of the `type` parameter. This means non-image attachments (e.g. `type=attachment`) supplied via `url` can now make the server download up to 10MB even on sites configured with a much smaller limit, and each such upload may additionally trigger five downsize conversions. The enlarged download bound should be applied only when the target is an image (and arguably should still be a configurable/site-derived limit), not to every API upload.

findings.title: Client validation no longer honors configured max size settings, including for attachments
findings.body: Replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` raises the client-side limit for every upload type. Only images are downsized server-side; attachments are still rejected by the server against `max_attachment_size_kb`. On a site configured with, say, a 1MB attachment limit, an 8MB PDF now passes `validateUploadedFile`, is uploaded, and only then fails with a server error. The message in `displayErrorForUpload` (line 246) has the same problem: the 413 case hardcodes 10MB and will report the wrong limit whenever the web-server threshold differs. The larger limit should be scoped to images (and ideally still derived from the site settings), leaving attachment limits unchanged.

findings.title: No tests cover the new automatic-downsize behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a new synchronous downsize loop plus a new `OptimizedImage.downsize` signature/overload, but no specs are included. There are no tests for: reaching the target size after N reductions, the loop giving up after 5 attempts, conversion failure (return false) being surfaced, the API-URL path, or animated GIFs via `downsize_instructions_animated`. The zero-arity/argument ambiguity between the two `downsize` definitions would also be caught by a simple unit test and currently is not.
